title: Publish SHA256SUMS.txt with every release
body:
## What

The release workflow's `publish` job now writes a `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering every release asset and uploads it with the other files.

- A new step runs `sha256sum` in `dist/` over the same file patterns the job already publishes (zip, setup.exe, tar.gz, deb, rpm, dmg, AppImage, snap, flatpak, pkg.tar.zst), checks the result with `sha256sum -c`, and prints it to the log.
- `dist/SHA256SUMS.txt` is added to the `softprops/action-gh-release` file list.

The file uses standard `sha256sum` format (`<hash>  <filename>`), so users can verify a download with:

```
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## Why

I've asked for CamCraft to be added to ArtCraft Launcher as a community app (storytold/craft-launcher#1545). The launcher checks every download, including downloads of community apps, against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so CamCraft can't be listed until its releases include one. Checksums also help anyone who downloads the files by hand.

Releases that are already published don't change. The file will appear starting with the next tag.

## Testing

- The YAML parses.
- I ran the step's script on sample files: it lists each asset once, `sha256sum -c` passes, and `release-body.md` isn't included.
- I haven't run it in a real release. That will happen on the next tag.

title: fix(3d): an Adaptive fallback to Offset rings raises a warning
body:
Stacked on #3062 (merge #3062 first).

This PR is partial work on #3035. It does the warning part only.

## What changed

- `camcraft_sim::verify::Warning` has a new variant, `StrategyFallback { at, areas }`.
  - It is advisory. `blocks_post` is false.
  - `at` is the first cutting move. `areas` is the number of areas that the Offset rings cut in place of the Adaptive plan.
- Generate (`operation/generate.rs`) counts the fallback notes and adds the warning when the count is more than zero.
  - The op now reports `warnings` > 0 in MCP `get_job` and `generate`.
  - MCP `verify` lists the finding as `strategy_fallback` with `blocks_post: false`.
  - The UI folds the warning on its own key (225).
- `machining2d::RINGS_FALLBACK` holds the note tail `" - Offset rings cut "`. The 2D door (`pocket_hsm`) and the 3D ladder (`machining3d::hsm::rings_tag`) both use it. `machining2d::rings_fallbacks` counts the notes by it. The note text does not change.
- The rest pass and the offset shells are not counted. Their Offset rings are by design, not a fallback.

## Cause

The planner wrote each fallback to Offset rings only into the path notes. The op status stayed `ok` with `warnings=0`. In the QA run, 14 levels fell back and nothing showed it except the notes.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `app strategy_fallback::an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning` (new). Before the fix it failed: `one fallback warning: []`, left 0, right 1.
  - `motion lib machining3d::hsm::fallback_tests::a_refused_level_counts_as_one_rings_fallback` (new).
- Mutations:
  - `generate.rs` from upstream/main (no guard): the app pin is red. Restored: green.
  - `rings_fallbacks` that matches nothing: the motion pin is red. Restored: green.
- Expected changes: these suites pinned "verifies clean" as zero warnings on fixtures that already fall back to rings. Each now allows only the fallback warning, and only when the notes name a fallback:
  - `adaptive_pinch`
  - `adaptive_zero_margin_island` (the MCP `findings` check skips `strategy_fallback` only)
  - `climb_direction`
  - `shoulder_adaptive`
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 312 steps. The first run had 4 red binaries, all from the new warning. After the test updates, the 4 binaries are green (`--failed` rerun).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. The posted G-code does not change.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. A heavy test that asserts zero warnings on an Adaptive op that falls back will now see one advisory warning.
- The QA part of #3035 (the mould core STL on len) did not run.
- Two parts of #3035 stay open:
  - the run time of Rough12, Rest6 and Waterline6 (5 to 13 min, or more);
  - a long generate that blocks every other MCP call, with no cancel tool.

## Overlaps

- #3062: the same function (`fold_warnings_located`, `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.
- #3080 and #2714 touch `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`, different variants and arms. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3103, #3033 and #2836 touch `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, other functions. #2836 adds `UndercutLift` on key 222; this PR uses 225.
- Many open PRs touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. This PR adds 7 lines after the drill-size law.

Effort: max (this part is smaller; the rest of #3035 stays at its label).

Changelog: An Adaptive operation that falls back to Offset rings now shows a warning with the number of areas, not only a note; the post is not held.

Refs #3035

title: fix(motion): turning offset claims a segment only where its tangent point lies on it
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: the line claim of a profile segment now holds only over its claim window. In that window the tangent point of the ball is on the segment. The claim window is the segment's station window, shifted by `d*b/sqrt(1 + b^2)`. At other stations, the circle about the nearer end point makes the claim.
- The OD ride (`profile_offset`) and the bore ride (`profile_offset_in`) use the same rule, through one private helper (`seg_claims`, `SegClaim`, `seg_range`).
- `seg_range` replaces the old probe of the ±1 neighbour segments. A shifted window can reach past the next segment.
- The two catalog programs `turning/cone-thread` and `turning/contour-finishes` are regenerated.
- `docs/decisions/2881-offset-tangent-window.md` records the decision.

## Cause

The old code held the infinite offset line of a segment over the segment's own station window. This is wrong in two directions:

- A steep, short chord claimed its line far above the bar. The first chord of a fillet has a slope of 16.6, so the claim was 167 mm too high (X354 on a 30 mm bar).
- A sloped face did not claim the stations before its inside corner, where it is the nearest piece. There the ride stood nearer than `d` to the face. This is a small gouge into the leave (0.884 instead of 1.0 at a 45 degree corner in the pin).

## Tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_window.rs`. Each test checks that every ride sample stands at exactly `d` from the profile:

- `a_steep_fillet_chord_keeps_the_ride_on_the_nose`: before the fix the max ride radius was 28.29 on an 11.66 profile.
- `a_sloped_inside_corner_is_not_gouged`: before the fix the ride stood 0.884 from the face at station -0.25.
- `the_inside_ride_obeys_the_same_window`: before the fix the bore ride dived to r 1.71 on an 18.34 wall.

Mutation checks:

- Old `offset.rs` put back: all 3 pins red. Restored: all 3 green.
- Sign of the window shift flipped: all 3 pins red. Restored: all 3 green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, `turning_bore`, `turning_offset_window`, `turning_prof`, app `example_catalog`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also run green in debug: app suites `turning_profile`, `turning_bore`, `turning_bore_feeds`, `turning_contour`, `turning_contour_stock`, `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_stock_approach`, `turning_hidden_floor`, `turning_insert_zone`, `turning_holder`, `turning_holder_steel`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_turn_radius`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_field_sim`, `recorded_post_streams`, `coarse_laws`, `coarse_rims`, `sim_lathe_body`, `ladder_entry_height`, `carried_stock_entry`, `stepped_stock_rapid`, `project_roundtrip`.

## Goldens moved

Two `.nc` files. The `.camproj` files do not change: the catalog tests pass with the committed projects.

- `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc`: at the cone-to-flat inside corner (Z59.2), each rough rung and the finish ride lose a run of zero-length `G01` blocks and a vertical drop. The new ride rolls over the corner on the nose circle (for example `G01 X28.532 Z59.697`, then `X28.5 Z60.194`). It stands slightly farther out than the old drop, which was inside the true offset.
- `examples/catalog/turning/contour-finishes/contour-finishes.nc`: near Z0 to Z1 the rides lose about 50 short blocks each that went out toward the spike of a steep chord. The clearance radius drops from `X22.884` to `X21.6`, and from `X20.762` to `X20.1` for the chamfer. The chamfer retract is now a short feed out to X20.1, then the rapid. The operation's own lead-out law makes this choice for the new, nearer clearance.

No other `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes. `cargo xtask gate heavy` reaches every app and motion heavy target for a change in `motion`. These were not run. Run them before the PR is flagged ready.
- The exact model of the issue (30 mm bar, 1.2 mm fillet). The pin uses the same chord slope in a hand-made profile.

## Overlaps

- #2897 (#2882) touches `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: the same file, different function (`thin`, and the final `Ok(...)` lines). It also regenerates `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc`. Whichever merges second refreshes and regenerates that golden.

Effort: high

Changelog: Turning profile rough and finish no longer ride far out of the bar at a steep fillet chord, and no longer ride inside the nose offset at a sloped inside corner.

Fixes #2881

title: feat(post): encode a zero-step Agie punch setup from main
body:
## Scope

Add a public `camcraft_post::agie_setup::PunchSetup20::encode` function. A Rust caller can pair its complete SBL piece script and SBR resource manifest with an existing ISO file. The caller supplies a program name, stock bounds and the position of the 2 mm threading hole in micrometres.

The encoder supports one closed punch in 20 mm steel 0001 with Berco 0.25 mm wire, Ra 0.30 and 1 mm separation. It binds the requested native quality and removes the erosion steps on import. The returned review text gives the expected offsets for the operator. The API does not generate, position or verify the caller's ISO contour. The caller must use the matching resource and check it in the control.

This branch starts directly from main at c5f4e6f94. It has no feature-stack commits, no new dependencies and no automatic machining option. The new function works independently of the CAMCraft workspace post. The first workspace writer must call this function and report the controller review before it can ship. The existing feature drafts need their own safety reviews.

## References

The MIT-licensed Agie Processor implementation supplied the Agie-specific interface reference. The contributor's team wrote that implementation. The license notice is in assets/ui/LICENSES.md. The two synthetic expected files come from the contributor's control-checked CCSEP20 example.

## Verification

The complete quick gate passed all 107 steps in 3.1 minutes on the final head befdc57f9. The complete reached heavy gate passed all 197 steps in 64.3 minutes. These commands also passed on that head:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base c5f4e6f94
cargo xtask gate heavy --base c5f4e6f94
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-post --doc agie_setup
cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

All four integration tests passed. The public API example compiled and ran. An independent Rust caller reproduced the complete CCSEP20.SBL and CCSEP20.SBR files byte for byte. On a copy of the actual offline control, the new piece had zero working steps. FORMALCHECK required the operator to define the technology. The work showed the intended punch, ISO, stock height and threading hole.

The pinning tests are:

- `setup_files_match_the_control_checked_zero_step_punch`
- `a_named_resource_and_signed_micron_coordinates_round_trip`
- `device_names_paths_and_script_text_cannot_enter_an_agie_record`
- `stock_and_full_start_hole_must_fit_the_setup_span`

No physical erosion was performed.

Effort: high
Changelog: The post library can encode a zero-step Agie setup for a qualified 20 mm punch with a caller-prepared ISO contour.

Refs #2984

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 687 steps.
  - The first full run had 685 ok and 2 red steps: `app build (--no-run)` and `app suites: break_through`. The cause was one test literal: the `strategy` field was in a Drill literal in `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`, not in the Bore literal.
  - After the fix, `--failed` on that run: 2 steps, 0 failed. The fix changed only that test file.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on the final head c70e84309: the motion and app heavy lanes, 231 steps, 0 failed (50.3 min).

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

Fixes #2830

title: fix(app): judge the mill kinds' first traverse on a mill-turn
body:
Stacked on #3097 (#3077). The diff against `main` also shows the commits of #3097. Review only the #3083 commits. Retarget this PR after #3097 merges.

## What changed

- `first_traverse::mill_order(kind, lathe_tool, params)` is new. It is true on a mill and on a mill-turn for a milling tool. A mill-turn posts a milling tool through the Fanuc mill post. That post sends Z to the clearance, then X/Y at that height (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`). This is the order that the first-traverse laws read.
- `generate.rs` reads `mill_order` in `turned_axis` and in the two `judge` calls, in place of `is_mill && !lathe_tool`. The planar, 3-D, hole and multi-axis kinds on a mill-turn now get the upright law, the 3+2 table law and the tip law. The laws do not change. The #3077 flag stays: `mill_order || mill_post_cross`.
- A rotary kind (`Mode::Rotary`) on a mill-turn stays out of the law. There it is a radial live tool on the spindle C, and the mill premise refuses each such program. Follow-up #3096 (P1) owns it.
- The struck-link planner and the mesh steel stay mill-only. The post gate judges each link of a mill-turn against the steel and refuses a struck link. The box verdict is stricter than the mesh verdict. Decision items 5 and 6 give the reasons.
- `current_stamp` writes the word `first-traverse-mill-turn-3083` for a judged mill kind on a mill-turn setup. Those caches read Stale one time. No stamp of a mill changes. No shipped example or catalog project mounts a mill-turn.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3083-mill-turn-first-traverse.md`. It states the premise: the start is at the tool-change height. A program that starts low is not covered.

## Readings

- 2D, refused: a steady with its top at Z40 and a face clearance of Z30 give `FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 30, top_mm: 40, fixture: true }`. The post refuses by name.
- 2D, clear: the same steady with its top at Z25 gives no warnings. The program is byte-identical to the bare program.
- 3+2 on the mill-turn's B at B10: clearance Z25 is refused, with the high corner of the stock at 5.209 mm along the tool axis. Clearance Z30 is clear.

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse_mill_turn::a_mill_turn_face_under_a_far_steady_holds_the_post_by_name`
- `first_traverse_mill_turn::a_mill_turn_face_over_a_low_steady_posts_the_bare_program`

title: fix(sim): judge the first traverse of a lathe or mill-turn cross drill from the turret's index position
body:
## What changed

A cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn now has a first-traverse law. Generation refuses a cross drill by name if its first rapid from the turret's index position can pass the work or the steel.

- **Premise.** The unknown start is the turret's index position, at the top of the X and Z travel. This is the premise of #2987 and of the upright law. A program that starts with the tool low near the work (for example after a manual jog) is not covered. The decision file says so.
- **The post's real first move.** `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` (lines 717-720) writes `G00 C`, then `G00 X Z` to the first motion record. The record stream writes the END of each move only (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:532-536`). The start of the first move goes out only as `StartX/Y/Z` (`mod.rs:274-280`), and `liveMove` does not move there. So the first G00 X Z goes to the R-plane point of the first hole.
- **The law** (`camcraft_sim::verify::live_first_traverse`, `crates/sim/src/verify/live_traverse.rs`).
  - A G00 moves each axis at its own rate. Thus the tip can pass every radius from the first point out, at every Z from the first point up, in the station's plane.
  - The tool lies along the radius. The swept solid follows the tool stack: flute, then shank, then holder, the widest band so far.
  - The work and the chuck are read at the C angle: each facet is clipped exactly.
  - Fixed steel (a tailstock, the table) is read revolved about the spindle.
  - A face that only touches the swept solid passes. The model excess follows the #1053 law.
- **Seam.** `crates/app/src/operation/cross_traverse.rs` is called in the cross branch of `generate.rs`. A hit gives `GenError::Invalid` with the solid's name, so nothing posts. A mill-turn cross drill also answers to the upright law, because its default post is the mill post.
- **Cache.** The cross drill's op stamp gets the word `live-traverse-3077`.
- **One test fixture changed** (coordinator decision, recorded in the decision file).
  - In `drilling_cross::recognition_finds_the_bar_two_holes_and_they_generate`, the 44 mm box stock stands out to X 22 from Z 0 up. At clearance 20, the first hole's R plane is at radius 20, Z -10. The first rapid's Z leg passes 2 mm of uncut stock, so the law refuses it correctly.
  - The test's clearance is now 30, which puts the R plane at radius 30. The test still pins the recognition and the generation.
  - Dropped: a rule that this stock is not there.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3077-lathe-cross-first-traverse.md`.

## Readings

- Example refusal: "the stock reaches out to 22.000 from the spindle at Z0.000" (the old recognition fixture).
- `coarse_cross_drill`: a flange flush with the R plane (x 20) is clear. Earlier drafts refused it.
- `drilling_cross_box`: the Ø12 shank stands 30 mm behind the tip and does not meet a lump 3 mm beside the drill's line. An earlier draft refused it.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_cross_drill.rs`:
  - `a_cross_drill_over_its_chuck_has_a_clear_first_traverse`
  - `a_cross_drill_under_a_wide_tailstock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_thin_tailstock_centre_is_clear_on_a_lathe_and_convicts_a_mill_turn`
  - `a_turning_collar_flush_with_the_first_point_is_clear_and_one_proud_of_it_is_refused`
- `crates/sim/src/verify/live_traverse_tests.rs`: 9 unit tests (tool width, touch, #1053 excess, shank band, half-plane, square bar, clipped facet, spindle off origin, unreadable input).

## Quick gate (local, debug)

- camcraft-sim lib `live_traverse`: 9 of 9 pass.
- camcraft-app on the final head: `drilling_cross` (9), `coarse_cross_drill` (6), `lathe_cross_drill` (9), `drilling_cross_box` (7) pass.
- camcraft-app on `37a84a2b5` (before the #1053 excess change and the fixture change): these binaries pass:
  - `cross_drill_neighbours`, `drill_reach`
  - `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_part`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `drilling_cross_stock`
  - `first_traverse_rotary`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `stock_source_cross_drill`
- The later changes apply the excess only when the model has one, and they change one test case.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
- The `operations` suite was not run on this head.
- The turret body is not modelled.
- The other mill-turn kinds stay outside this law (#3083).

Note: PR #3093 (#3081) also changes `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`. This PR does not change that file. It changes the call at the upright judge in `generate.rs`.

Changelog: A cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn is refused by name when its first rapid from the turret's index position can pass the stock, a part, a chuck or a tailstock.

title: fix(app): refuse a 3+2 down-pointing tool axis that can go under the table

## What changed

Past a 90-degree head tilt, the tool axis of a 3+2 plane points down toward the machine table. The move from the tool-change height along that axis to the clearance plane can end under the table top. Before this PR, #2987 gave only a note in that case, and the post did not stop.

- `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`: new `Warning::FirstTraverseUnderTable { at, height_mm, limit_mm }`. The text says "lower the clearance plane to Z<limit> or under it". It never says "raise". The verdict blocks the post (`blocks_post` is true).
- `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`: `TableRead::Unjudged` is now `Under { limit }`, with `limit = low + stroke / -axis_z` (`low` is the lowest start reading along the axis). `judge` pushes this verdict beside the stock and fixture verdict. The note is removed.
- `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`: the salt `first-traverse-table-3081` is added for each operation with a tilt. A tilted cache that the old law judged reads Stale one time. Without the salt, an old cache keeps the note, has no verdict, and posts.
- Exhaustive matches: `warned_moves.rs`, `mcp/job.rs` (kind `first_traverse_under_table`), and `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` (fold key 224 and `last_move`). Key 222 is used by open PR #2836 and key 223 by open PR #3062, so this PR uses 224.
- Examples: the tilted operations of `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.camproj`, `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` and `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` are restamped. Only the stamps change. Regenerated by the new law, the warnings, notes and moves are the same (max deviation 5e-7 mm, the rounding of the file). No `.nc` file changes.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3081-table-down-axis-verdict.md`. It uses the premise of #2987: the unknown start is at the tool-change height (the Z travel top). The law does not cover a program that starts with the tool low near the table.

## Readings

B 120 on the test machine (X +-400, Z stroke 300): the limit is 113.590 along the axis. A plane at 150 is refused. Planes at 100 and 113 pass.

## Pinning tests

title: fix(verify): a tilted plane reads its stock cap in its own frame
body:
## What changed

- The tilted (3+2) verify branch in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` starts its local stock cap at negative infinity.
- The cap is the maximum local height of the projected stock box and model box corners.
- The world stock top (`stock_top_z - oz`) is no longer a lower bound for the local cap.
- A new suite `crates/app/tests/tilt_stock_cap.rs` pins the fix.
- A decision file `docs/decisions/3004-local-stock-cap.md` records the choice.

## Cause

`stock_top_z` is a height along world Z.
The tilted branch used it, minus the plane origin's Z, as the start value of the local cap.
The projected corners could only raise this value.
On a side plane (A +90 or A -90) of a 60 x 60 x 70 blank, the real local cap is 30.
The cap stayed at 70.
The shank law then named a shank 11 mm over the side face a `ShankHit`.
The first-traverse law named a clearance 10 mm over the face low (`FirstTraverseLow`, `top_mm: 70`).
The rapid law named the drop to the face `RapidInStock`.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/tilt_stock_cap.rs` (each runs at A +90 and A -90, with the issue's blank and `EM-0600-4FL`):

- `a_side_pocket_reads_the_local_stock_cap_not_the_world_top`: a 4 mm side pocket. No `ShankHit`. Red before the fix: `[ShankHit { at: 2, part: false }, ShankHit { at: 3, .. }, ShankHit { at: 4, .. }, ShankHit { at: 5, .. }, FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 40.0, top_mm: 70.0, .. }]`.
- `a_side_slot_reads_its_clearance_against_the_local_cap`: a 4 mm side slot. No warnings. Red before the fix: `[RapidInStock { at: 1 }, FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 40.0, top_mm: 70.0, fixture: false }]`.
- `a_shank_that_enters_the_side_face_still_convicts`: a 20 mm side pocket. The shank foot is 5 mm under the face. `ShankHit` stays. Green before and after.

Mutation check: with `generate.rs` from upstream/main, the first two pins fail and the third passes. With the fix, all three pass.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (117 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. The fix changes warnings only. It does not change a toolpath.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run.
- An oblique plane (not a multiple of 90 degrees) keeps the conservative box cap. The issue names this as a separate limitation.
- A material with no facets gives an inverted model box. Its projected corners give a very high cap (an over-report), as before. No test covers this case.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch `generate.rs`, in different lines of `run_job_arms`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

- #2997 and #3082: the `first_traverse::Over` line that reads `st_local`.
- #3087: the `fidelity_law::tightened` lines.
- #3065, #3059, #3058: other lines of the same file.

Changelog: A 3+2 side operation (A +90 / A -90) reads the stock's cap along its own tool axis, so a shank or clearance clear of the side face is no longer named a collision.

Fixes #3004

title: fix(import): refuse a STEP item with no unit context in a degree file
body:
## What changed

- `crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs` gets `UnlistedAngles`. It finds the first stated plane angle unit that is not the radian. It also finds the items that a representation with a context lists, and the pieces of those solids.
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs` (`read_guarded`) uses it after the topology read:
  - A built solid with no unit context is refused when the file states a non-radian angle unit.
  - For an item that failed to read, the unit reason replaces the read message. The wrong angle unit is the first cause of the failure.
- A file that states only the radian, or no angle unit, keeps such an item.
- The refusal names the item and the angle unit, for example: `no representation gives it a unit context, so its angles would be read in radians, but the file states plane angle unit #13, which is not the radian`.

## Cause

The pinned reader gives a solid item that no representation lists the default units: 1 mm per length unit and 1 radian per angle unit. Nothing checked the angle default. In a degree file, the reader read the angles of that item in radians, without a warning.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/kernel/tests/step_short_units.rs`:

- `unlisted_item_in_a_degree_file_is_refused_by_name`: the degree cone fixture with the solid #16 not listed. Red before the fix: the item was refused for an edge gap (`face #40: an edge lies 8.32 mm off the face's surface`), not for its unit.
- `unlisted_item_that_reads_cleanly_is_refused_by_name`: the same cone with a semi-angle that reads cleanly in radians. Without the fix it imports as a wrong solid (volume 3196.7 mm^3, no warning).
- `unlisted_item_in_a_radian_file_is_kept`: control. A millimetre and radian cube with no context imports as a 1 mm cube.

Mutation results:

- Solid filter disabled: `unlisted_item_that_reads_cleanly_is_refused_by_name` is red (the wrong cone imports). Restored: green.
- Failure message mapping removed: `unlisted_item_in_a_degree_file_is_refused_by_name` is red. Restored: green.
- Radian rule removed (each angle unit counts as non-radian): `unlisted_item_in_a_radian_file_is_kept` is red. Restored: green.

None.

- A file with an unlisted surface model (a sheet) in a degree file. The same filter covers it, because the reader gives sheets in `read.solids`.

PR #2927 has `needs-rework` and `conflicts`, so this PR does not stack on it. Whichever merges second refreshes.

title: fix(sim): judge a reduced-accuracy model at its own chord error, up to 0.02 mm
body:
## What changed

- **The law** (`crates/sim/src/verify/excess.rs`). `excess_floor` reads a model's chord error `c` in three ranges:
  - `c` up to `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm): the whole excess is taken (#864, no change).
  - `c` from 0.01 mm to `WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT` (0.02 mm): only the promised chord (0.005 mm) is taken. The program verdict is then read at the model's own chord error.
  - `c` over 0.02 mm: the whole excess is taken, so nothing is left. The operation is refused by name.
- `WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT` is a constant. No file, facet budget or vouch can raise it.
- A tolerance is never made larger than the law's own tolerance.
- **Collision bands** grow by the whole excess (`verify::band_growth`). The widening is never given to a band.
- **Strict readers** keep #864's law (`verify::strict_floor`, `fidelity_law::tightened_strict`):
  - the turning margin, the lathe axial-hole tolerance and `revolve::gouge_tol_on`;
  - the rotary field allowances;
  - the probe stylus slack.

  The program gate reads the strict law for these kinds (`fidelity_law::widens`).
- **Header note.** `ProgramId` has `notes`. The engine writes each note through the script's `onComment`, after `onOpen`. `document_program_id` fills the notes from `fidelity_note::program_notes`. Example: `Reduced accuracy: model brick was checked to 0.019 mm, not 0.010 mm`.
- **Notes in plain words.** The model summary, the MCP `facts` note and the #2994 import note (`step::loosened_consequence`) say the same fact.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2996-wide-verdict.md`. It gives the rule for each direction, each reader, what the user loses, and what was dropped.

## Cause

The #864 law took the whole excess from each tolerance. At a chord of 0.02 mm the excess is 0.015 mm. That is more than `DEV_TOL`, so no tolerance was left. Each finishing operation on such a model was refused at the post.

## Tests

New pins:
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity_wide.rs`:
  - `a_model_just_under_the_limit_posts_an_exact_finish_with_a_header_note` (0.019 mm).
  - `a_model_just_over_the_limit_is_refused_by_name` (0.021 mm).
  - `a_real_gouge_deeper_than_the_verdict_tolerance_still_blocks_a_widened_model` (0.02 mm under the face).
  - `the_edge_gap_step_file_opened_at_reduced_accuracy_posts_a_face_with_the_note` (the #2994 fixture `edge_gap_018_stated_010.step`).
  - `a_full_fidelity_model_and_a_mild_one_say_nothing_new`.
- `crates/sim/tests/model_excess.rs`: `past_dev_tol_up_to_the_limit_only_the_promised_chord_is_taken`, `a_cut_deeper_than_the_widened_tolerance_into_a_convex_wall_is_still_convicted`.
- `crates/app/tests/coarse_laws.rs`: a rotary op on a 0.019 mm model is still refused by name.

Mutation checks (each restored after):
1. `excess_floor` takes the whole excess again: 2 app pins and 2 sim pins go red.
2. `band_growth` reads the widened tolerance: `past_dev_tol_...` and `full_fidelity_grows_nothing` go red.
3. The engine writes no notes: the header pin goes red.
4. Every kind widens: the rotary pin goes red.

Pins changed on purpose (the old formula for a chord past `DEV_TOL`): `model_fidelity` (TIGHT), `fidelity_copies`, `coarse_probe_plasma` (plasma kerf), `import_step_edge_gap` (note text), and the sim `model_excess`, `coarse_collision` and `boundary_arc_walls`. The `coarse_collision` loops now use an excess past the limit. An excess of 0.01 mm is now judged, and those cases convict.

Full-fidelity pins: unchanged and green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head before the main merge: 254 steps, 2 red. Both were pins of the old formula, fixed in 5eef00704.
- On the final head, the gate ran steps 1-128 (post, kernel, sim, motion) green. At step 129 (app build), the gate's sccache wrapper hung on `ring`'s `curve25519.c` two times. I stopped it.
- I then ran the same binaries with plain cargo (`env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER`): all 601 `camcraft-app` lib and test binaries, and the 6 ui binaries that the gate selects. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. The change reaches them. This PR is not ready until they run.

title: fix(sim): judge the first traverse of the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds
body:
Stacked on #2997. GitHub cannot base a PR on a fork branch, so the diff below also shows the commits of #2997 (branch `mkinney:issue/2987-table-tilted-first-traverse`, merged here at 05c9e56f2). Merge #2997 first. Then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and only its own commits stay.

## What changed

After a tool change the post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the block with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `xyFirst`, `traverseZ`, `onRapid`). The Z of that traverse is the higher of the clearance height and the start. The #2901 law did not judge the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds. Now each kind has a law or a named refusal:

- **Rotary kinds** (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset): the new law `sim::verify::first_traverse_low_swept`.
  - The rotary words come after the X/Y traverse, so the law reads the work swept through a full turn about the fitted axis. It reads the stock and part points, and the steel that turns with the work (a chuck), at its corners.
  - It reads the fixed steel (table, tailstock) at its machine-frame top.
  - It reads the start at its machine height over the axis line, lifted to the clearance height.
  - The mounted machine selects the law. A machine whose work tilts gets the swept law. A machine whose head tilts gets the tip law. An unstated or mixed machine gets both laws.
  - When no axis can be fitted, generation is refused by name.
- **Multi-axis kinds** (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour): the #2901 law on the tip in the part frame, at the post's traverse height.
- **Cross drill on a mill**: generation refuses it by name before any move ("cross holes are live-tooling work"). A test pins this refusal.
- **Cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn**: this law does not judge it. The decision file records the limit. Refs #3077, which owns the gap.
- **Verdict**: the same blocking `Warning::FirstTraverseLow`. The post gate, the UI, MCP and the warned moves do not change.
- **Cache**: the op stamp of these kinds gets one more word (`first-traverse-2965`). Such a cache reads Stale once. The salt stays at v4, so no other stamp moves.

Dropped options: a reading at the start angle only (the rotary words come after the traverse); a sweep for the multi-axis kinds (no axis line is stated for them); a blanket refusal; a new `Warning` variant; a salt bump to v5 for all kinds. The decision file has the reasons: `docs/decisions/2965-first-traverse-rotary.md`.

## Examples (stamp-only regeneration, accepted by the maintainer)

- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` (Journal) and `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (Swarf1) were regenerated. Only the operation `stamp` field of each file changes (`git diff --word-diff`).

  - `a_radial_start_reads_its_radius_over_the_axis_line`
  - `a_chuck_turns_with_the_work_and_a_tailstock_stands_still`
  - `the_swept_top_follows_the_axis_tilt_and_refuses_no_input`

title: fix(turning): refuse a helical modelled thread by name
body:
## What changed

- New detector `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_helix::helix`. It finds a helical surface (a modelled screw thread) from the facet normal lines. It gives the axis, the pitch and the hand.
- Threading now refuses a model with a helical thread. The message names the helical thread, its pitch and its hand. It tells the user to model the thread as revolved V grooves.
- The refusal is in the kernel (`turning::helical_refusal`, called by `thread_planned_in`). It is also in the app Threading arm, before the slice of the job region.
- `axis.rs`: the facet-datum loop and the normal moment move into two helpers (`data_of`, `moment`). The axis fit does not change.

## Cause

Threading reads a modelled thread as a revolved V section. A helical thread has no such section. Two earlier steps refused the issue's part with messages that named other causes:

- STEP route: the slice of the job region said `the mesh is open ... dangling chord ends`.
- Native route: the axis fit did not accept the helical flanks and said `every axis fits this model equally`. When the axis fit passes, the kernel said `nothing to thread ... threading cuts a MODELED thread`, and that does not tell the user that the thread is helical.

## How the detector works

About a candidate axis `(o, u)`, each inclined facet gives the screw parameter `h = (n x u) . (o - p) / (n . u)`. The normal lines of a helical surface belong to a linear line complex (Pottmann & Wallner, Computational Line Geometry). A revolve gives `h = 0`. The two flanks of a helical thread give one common nonzero `h`. The gates are:

- The agreeing area is at least half of the inclined area and at least 2% of the part.
- The agreeing facets go all the way round the axis (the coarseness skip of `axis.rs`).

The pitch is the area-weighted mean of the agreeing band. The two triangles of one twisted quad read `h` low and high (1.356 and 1.665 for a 1.5 pitch), so the median would be about 10% low.

## Tests

The QA files of the issue were not on this machine. The pins use a procedural shaft of the same shape: an M16x1.5 helical V, a Ø24 body and a Ø30 head, 70 long.

- `camcraft-motion` `turning_thread_helical`:
  - `a_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_left_hand_helical_thread_says_left_hand`
  - `a_coarse_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name` (48 segments)
  - `an_open_helical_mesh_is_refused_by_name` (facets removed)
  - `a_revolved_v_thread_and_a_smooth_bar_are_not_helical` (the pitch is found to 2%)
- `camcraft-app` `turning_thread_helical`:
  - `a_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name_before_the_slice` (an open mesh, as the STEP route)

Mutation results:

- The upstream kernel (`thread.rs`, `turning/mod.rs`) makes the four motion refusal pins fail with `nothing to thread - no valley 0.920 down ... threading cuts a MODELED thread` or `no material crosses the station interval`. My code makes them pass.
- The upstream `generate.rs` (no app guard) makes the app pin fail with `M16: the source model cannot be sliced: the mesh is open at z = 2.1875: 12 dangling chord ends`. This is the message in the issue. My code makes it pass.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (160 steps, 0 failed). This includes all the `turning_thread*` suites, and they keep their revolved-V fixtures. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. After the gate run, I changed only lints (`is_multiple_of`, a collapsed `if let`). Then I ran the two pin files again (green) and clippy again (clean).

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The issue's real STEP and `.sc` models (`/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/`). The files were not on this machine. A reviewer on skull can run `open_project` and `generate {name:"M16Modeled"}` / `generate {name:"M16Native"}` and expect the `HELICAL` refusal.
- A reader for helical threads (a phase from the helix) is not part of this PR. It is new algorithm work and changes posted G-code.
- This PR does not repair the STEP tessellation gaps of helical faces. That is an importer defect. Threading now refuses before the slice.
- No heavy lane ran.

## Overlaps

- Open PRs that change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` in other functions: #3059, #3058, #2997, #2920, #2890, #2836, #2831, #2822, #2716, #2714. None changes the Threading arm. Touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis.rs` grows from 411 to 422 lines. The cause is the two extracted helpers. The file was already above 400 lines before this PR.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3023-helical-thread-refusal.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Threading refuses a model with a helical modelled thread with a message that names the helical thread, its pitch and its hand, in place of a slice or axis-fit error.

Fixes #3023

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.

Clip each pick-outline segment before screen projection.

- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_mesh_stays_within_the_rectangle_stroke`

- `SetOperationSetup` gives the moved operation a position at the end of its target setup.

title: fix(post): a symlinked executable finds the assets beside the real file
body:
## What changed

- `DataFiles::from_process` (`crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`) resolves the executable path with the new `real_exe` before the assets lookup. If the path is a symbolic link, `real_exe` gives the real file (`std::fs::canonicalize`). The lookup then starts in the install folder, not in the folder of the link. The posts and the machines use this lookup.
- `real_exe` changes only a link. A plain path keeps its form, so a Windows path in a message gets no `\\?\` prefix. A link that does not resolve keeps the link path, and the refusal names the folder of the link, as before.
- The refusal of a copy of the executable now ends with `COPY_HINT`: "Start the program from its install folder, or through a symbolic link to the installed executable: a copy of the executable has no assets beside it." No setting or environment variable points at an assets folder, so the hint names none.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3028-symlink-exe-posts.md`.

## Readings (Linux, Manjaro, release build of `camcraft-cli`)

Install-style folder: `install/camcraft-cli` and `install/assets/{posts,machines}`, outside a cargo build tree. Command: `camcraft-cli process examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.camproj -o out.nc`.

| Started as | Before this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| `install/camcraft-cli` | rc 0, 369 lines | rc 0, 369 lines |
| `bin/camcraft-cli`, a symbolic link to the installed file | rc 0, 369 lines | rc 0, 369 lines, the same bytes as the install run |
| `copy/camcraft-cli`, a copy | rc 1, "no posts folder found ..." | rc 1, the same refusal, then the `COPY_HINT` text |

On Linux, `current_exe` reads `/proc/self/exe`, which is already the real file. Thus the symlink case worked on Linux before this change. The fix is for macOS and Windows, where `current_exe` gives the link path.

## Pinning tests

- `data_dir::tests::a_symlinked_exe_finds_the_assets_beside_the_real_file` (Unix only: a symbolic link on Windows needs a privilege). It also checks a chain of two links, a dangling link, and the old result for the link path.
- `data_dir::tests::a_copied_exe_is_refused_with_the_fix`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (`post build`, `post suites: lib`, `post suites: folder_scan`).

title: fix(2d): keep contour leads on the air side at a closed ring's seam
body:
## What changed
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_fit.rs`: a new function `seam_tangents` gives the lead-in and lead-out tangents. `plan_leads` and `both_fit` use it.
- On a closed ring, it compares the start tangent and the end tangent at the seam.
- If the ring bends to the air side at the seam, the lead-out tangent is mirrored across the start tangent. The lead-in tangent is mirrored across the end tangent.
- Then each lead leaves the seam on the air side of the whole ring.
- A smooth seam, a seam that bends away from the air, and an open walk (tab windows, chains, an exit point) keep their tangents.
- New test file `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/3019-contour-tab-lead-cross.md`.

## Cause
- The seam of a round-cornered outside ring falls on a fitted corner arc.
- The arc's end tangent is about 0.05 degree off the ring's first chord, toward the material.
- The 8 mm linear lead-out goes along that tangent. It crosses the ring's second move about 0.25 mm past the seam.
- The crossing law found this on each level. This is the issue's "feed moves 5 and 13 cross" (one pair on each level).
- Tabs are not the cause. The same crossing occurs with no tabs.
- On a conventional cut, the lead-in has the same fault against the ring's last move.
- The crossing law is correct and does not change.

## Tests
Pins (the issue's plate: 120 x 80, four R6 corners, D10 tool, stepdown 3, 12 deep, 4 tabs 3 x 1, linear lead 8):
- `an_outside_tabbed_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing` (climb, 4 tabs).

body:
## Review fixes and final-head validation

Final head: `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`. Base: `upstream/main` at `211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6`.

1. Full circles split into two half arcs before chord generation. Both directions retain the complete cut. Pin: `linearize_full_circles_keeps_both_directions`.
2. Work-offset and XY-origin changes clear the rapid cache. The next rapid precedes the jet-on words. Pin: `waterjet_rapid_cache_resets_when_the_coordinate_frame_changes`.
3. The machine mirror preserves the waterjet kind. The CLI test uses a vendor tree with linear axes. Pin: `the_cli_posts_a_vendor_tree_waterjet_machine`.
4. Arc generation refuses a chord tolerance that the subdivision cap cannot meet. Pin: `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_tolerance_below_the_chord_cap`.

All four pins pass. Each fix was removed separately. Each pin then failed an assertion with exit 101. Each restored fix passed.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. The CL change selects the batch plan. All 997 steps pass in 35.4 minutes.
- Clippy: GREEN in 142 seconds. Command: `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. All reached app and motion lanes ran. There are 234 steps, with one failed step, in 42.0 minutes.
- The failed heavy step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. Its failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`.
- That test also fails on the original PR head `fe3c8f6e029a44ddae4a4c5d0f93f95d58b60d9f`. Both heads produce `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. The Linux assertion expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`. The baseline run exits 101 at the same assertion.

The heavy gate is not green. This patch does not change the unrelated path-count assertion. The PR remains a draft.

The earlier test results below describe the original implementation. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

title: fix(post): scale output budget with the input program
body:
## What changed

The post engine scales its output budget with the parsed input record count.
The budget is `max(100_000, 16 * records + 1_024)`, capped at `u32::MAX` with saturating arithmetic.
A Tormach operation with 100,001 feed moves now posts whole and per operation.
An output refusal states the limit, attempted line count, and operation.

The emitter keeps a private counter.
The host preserves a refusal after a script catches the exception or resets its public counters.
Direct output buffer writes use the same budget.
The output extraction helper moves into `js_host` to keep `js.rs` below 400 lines.

## Cause

The runaway guard used a fixed 100,000-line cap for every input size.
A valid operation could exceed this cap by itself.
The error gave no limit, count, or operation.

title: feat(mcp): compact read modes and chat context budgets
body:
## What changed

MCP read modes for small context windows (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`. Each operation keeps only the `params` fields that differ from the kind defaults. Null and empty fields outside `params` are removed.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (key or label) and `section`. An unknown name is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the name and the pick facts. Counts replace the loops. The compact default `limit` is 25. The full default stays 500.
- `provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet::Core)` gives a core set of 25 workflow tools. `tools(provider)` is unchanged.
- The new code is in `mcp/compact.rs`. `job.rs`, `features.rs`, `pick.rs` and `tools.rs` get small hooks only.

Chat worker limits (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):

- A tool reply to the model is cut at 12000 JSON characters, with a hint that names the compact modes. The tool card keeps the full text.
- A request carries at most one viewport image (the newest).
- A turn stops after 12 model rounds. The old `MAX_TURN_STEPS` moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and now has a test.
- A request carries at most 6 earlier turns. When older turns are dropped, the latest `get_job` reply goes in front of the first kept prompt.
- A local endpoint gets the core tool set. A cloud endpoint gets the full table.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1944-ai-context-budgets.md`.

title: fix(app): judge the first traverse of a 3+2 plane against the machine table
body:
Stacked on #2985 (merge #2985 first). This PR has one commit of its own on top of the #2985 head `73e10f954`: `7e6e2ffe3`.

## What changed

- The first-traverse law (#2985) now reads the machine table on a 3+2 plane. Before, it skipped the table in each tilted frame.
- The law reads the table's top face over the stated X/Y travel. The table box is clipped to the Z travel, which starts at the table top. The 1e6 mm slab under the top face is out of the tool's reach.
- The law reads the table only when the head can tilt. The machine file states which rotaries turn the work (`turns_part`, #804). When each tilting rotary turns the work, the table stays under the work, and the law does not read the table.
- A mounted machine that states no X, Y and Z travel has no table box. A 3+2 plane on such a machine gets a note: "First traverse: the machine table is not judged on this tilted plane: ...". It is not a silent pass.
- Files: `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (the predicate `work_tilts`, the clip `table_top_face`, the note), and `generate.rs` (passes the rotary list, adds the note to the path).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2987-table-tilted-first-traverse.md`.

## Cause

- #2985 skipped the table in a tilted frame. A full read of the table box refused each indexed operation on the microARC 4.
- I measured why. A read of the top face alone still refused them: Z 190.5 at A 90 and Z 336.55 at A 180. Those refusals are false. The microARC 4 turns the work, so its table never stands over the plane.
- On a head-tilt machine the table is fixed in the world. The tilted plane drops toward it on its low side. That collision passed.

## Tests

New file `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`. It uses a small test machine (X and Y travel +-100 mm, Z travel 0..300 mm) with three rigs: head tilt, work tilt, and head tilt with no travel.

- `a_head_tilt_plane_under_the_table_inside_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`: B 30 deg, plane 20 mm over the origin, table top face at 32.68 mm along the axis. The verdict is `FirstTraverseLow { fixture: true }` and the post is refused by name. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_machine_with_no_travel_names_the_table_unjudged`: the note is on the path. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_past_90_reads_the_table_top_face_not_its_slab`: B 120 deg. A plane 100 mm over the origin passes, and a plane 90 mm over it is refused at the top face (96.6 mm).
- `a_head_tilt_plane_over_the_table_top_face_passes`: control.
- `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work`: control, the same plane as the refused case.

Mutation checks (each run, then restored):
- The old `first_traverse.rs` and `generate.rs` from #2985: the refusal pin and the note pin fail.
- No top-face clip (the full slab): `a_head_tilt_past_90_reads_the_table_top_face_not_its_slab` fails.
- `work_turns = false`: `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` fails.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2985` (the #2985 head; my diff only): 116 steps, 0 failed.
- These suites passed separately (45 binaries): `first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `tilt`, `tilt_a180`, `tilt_a180_routes`, `tilt_heights`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `stock_source_holes`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_router_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, the `wcs_*` suites and others.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. The indexed example operations that posted on #2985 still post.

## Not exercised

- App heavy lanes: the [reviewer ran `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2997#issuecomment-7045080077) on this head trial-merged with main at `97a880c53`: 199 steps, 198 ok, 1 failed (`pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`). The reviewer reproduced the same failure with main's `first_traverse.rs` and `generate.rs`, so the failure is not from this PR.
- No machine run.
- The law runs at generation only (as in #2985). If the user loads a different machine after a generate, the first traverse is not judged again until the next generate. This gap is in #2985's design and also applies to the fixtures.
- A machine with a head tilt and a vertical work C: the table footprint is read without the C turn.
- An old project whose rotary has no `turns_part` is read as a head tilt (the conservative reading). It can be refused where it posted on #2985.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #2985: the same function `operation::first_traverse::judge` and the `Over` struct. #2985 adds the file.
- No other open PR changes these files.

Changelog: The first rapid of a 3+2 operation on a head-tilt machine is now refused by name when its clearance plane goes under the machine table top inside the machine travel; a machine that states no travel gets a note that the table was not judged.

body:
## What changed

Add `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket` with an original U-shaped open pocket.
Include the mesh generator, mesh, build script, portable project, NC program, and README.
Run 2D Adaptive before 2D Pocket with the same 6 mm end mill.
Adaptive leaves 0.5 mm on the walls and floor.
Pocket removes these allowances and reaches Z6.
The README explains the extra corner scallops and material left in sharp corners.

## Cause

The catalog had no case for Adaptive roughing followed by Pocket finishing.
The existing commands already support this sequence.
No machining algorithm changes are needed.

## Tests

- Pin: `adaptive_pocket_case_roughs_above_the_finished_floor_then_finishes`.
- The pin failed before the case existed. It passes with the case.
- Mutation: remove the new NC file to restore the upstream absence. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Adaptive wall allowance from 0.5 to 0. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Adaptive bottom from Z6.5 to Z6. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Pocket wall allowance from 0 to 0.5. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Pocket bottom from Z6 to Z6.5. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: all six cases pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: all five tests pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all three steps pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes.

The new case has no prior file on `upstream/main` to restore with `git show`.
Each mutation restores the exact original fixture bytes.
The pin checks operation types, order, allowances, posted depths, and model portability.
The catalog tests regenerate, verify, rebuild from the script, and compare NC bytes.

## Goldens moved

One new golden: `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.nc`.
It contains 13,325 lines for Adaptive roughing to Z6.5 and Pocket finishing to Z6.
The diff adds only this case's program. No existing NC or CL golden changes.

## Not exercised

No physical CNC machine was run.
Both operations omit a holder.
Verification checks for gouges. It does not prove complete stock removal.
The cutter leaves material in sharp inside corners.
Pocket recuts the selected region. This case does not demonstrate rest machining.

## Overlaps

None. The pin uses a new test file and leaves the shared catalog test unchanged.

Effort: medium

This change builds on the machine template in #2948 and the standalone encoder in #3104. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...5bdbb5fe43c8c09d0e1ea7ab9c7510e1e950abd7).

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

On the corrected writer, the normal CLI produced the same three CCSEP20 files as the independently verified import in #3104. Only the output stem was changed from the PUNCH40 example. The copy of the actual control showed the closed punch at zero steps. FORMALCHECK blocked it until the operator assigns technology. See [the file hashes and native work details](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3104#issuecomment-7055077111). The native bytes were tested once in that replay. No physical cut was made.

On successive imports, select the newly created piece. Match its ISO, start hole and zero steps to the intended setup. Verify the effective wire, height, quality and offsets before assigning TECCUT. Run the control's graphic and formal checks on the resulting steps.

On the earlier writer, the control plotted a rough pass and three trims after automatic generation. The measured offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. That historical result does not qualify an automatic release on this or another installation.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Final head checks

At a08c802b6, all five writer tests, four standalone encoder tests and ten application integration tests passed. The normal PUNCH40 script reproduced the previous guarded ISO, SBR and SBL. A repeat export refused to replace them. Both PUNCH40 and the CCSEP20 variant returned `working_steps_generated=false` and the controller review.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib agie::tests::
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native
```

Pinning tests include `script_post_reports_the_required_control_review_and_zero_working_steps`, `stock_origin_and_fractional_setup_coordinates_are_refused_before_publication`, `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch` and `qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition`.

The final head is 5bdbb5fe4. It includes the upstream diagnostic fix from #3092 and a dedicated recorded-stream suite for the Agie dispatcher. The single-file post entry point must refuse the Agie dispatcher. Each of 11 input streams checks the diagnostic, the failure exit code and the absence of NC output. The suite inventory also requires this post to have its own tests.

On this exact head the recorded suite passed 12/12 tests. The dispatcher suite passed 11/11. All nine default-machine regression tests and all 19 native tests passed. The normal CLI and an independent Rust caller reproduced the checked setup files and the matching ISO. Both duplicate exports preserved all files. Against upstream 211105042, the full plan selects 1,017 quick steps and 251 reached heavy steps. These two full gates have no completed result on this head.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test default_machine_missing
```

The compiled desktop picker and receipt were checked locally on the safety-adoption source a08c802b6. The picker identifies Ra as requested. The receipt shows the ISO, threading-hole and working-step checks, the TECCUT assignment and the required offsets. Updated screenshots remain local for review.
